newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian 1997 deficit to be 2.8 pct-budget minister.
newsitem.headline: Belgian 1997 deficit to be 2.8 pct-budget minister.

text.p: Belgium's 1997 budget deficit will be 2.8 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Budget Minister Herman Van Rompuy said.
"It is certainly 2.8, we now have sufficient details," Van Rompuy told BRTN radio.
Van Rompuy said Belgium would not have to impose extra budget savings in 1997 to reach the 2.8 percent deficit/GDP ratio, which virtually guaranteed its entry in EMU.
"I think we meet all the conditions, and also the international media believe...we will 100 percent certainly participate in the European monetary union," Van Rompuy said.
The government will discuss Van Rompuy's forecast later on Friday at the last cabinet meeting before the summer break.
The Belgian central bank had also predicted a deficit/GDP ratio of 2.8 percent for 1997, slightly above a European Union forecast of 2.7 percent.
